# Incident Report: MTA-2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.21.58 |
| MAC address | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (NetBIOS also broadcasts as WIN11OFFICE) |
| Logged-in user | `gwyatt` (Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM) |
| Domain controller | 10.1.21.2 (LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic target) |

## Malware Family / Attribution
No IDS/Suricata artifacts were provided alongside the PCAP, so attribution is **behavioral only, not signature-confirmed**.

The traffic profile matches a **fingerprinting-gated browser stealer/loader**, consistent with the delivery and check-in pattern used by commodity stealers such as Lumma/Vidar-class malware (fake file-hosting delivery → hidden-browser fingerprint collection → tokenized check-in). I cannot assert a specific named family with certainty since no packer/binary signature, YARA hit, or unique C2 protocol marker is present in traffic alone — this is a behavioral classification.

**Observed infection chain (all times UTC+4 per capture, 2026-01-28):**
1. `03:04:49.2` — victim browses `hiyter.com` (104.21.22.231) immediately after a Google query, then `media.megafilehub4.lat` (104.21.48.156) — a fake file-hosting/SEO-poisoned download page.
2. `03:04:52.3` — victim's browser opens a TLS session to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67, port 443, Cloudflare ECH-obscured SNI) and pulls down a **16 MB payload** — by far the largest single flow in the capture (19,722 frames / 16 MB down). Content is fully TLS-encrypted; no filename or hash is recoverable from ciphertext.
3. `03:05:36` (~42s later, after execution) — victim contacts `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156), then `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) over **plaintext HTTP on port 80**.
4. Victim's system performs a scripted browser-fingerprinting check-in against `whitepepper.su`: `GET /api/set_agent?id=...&token=...&agent=Chrome`, followed by a `POST ...&act=log` whose body is a URL-encoded JSON blob containing `navigator.userAgent/platform/hardwareConcurrency/deviceMemory`, WebGL vendor/renderer, canvas fingerprint, screen/WebRTC data. The same id/token pair is replayed for `agent=Edge`, indicating enumeration of multiple installed browsers.
5. Later in the session (`~03:06:15` / frame ~27833-28006), the host also reaches `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24) and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36) — consistent with malvertising/scareware redirect infrastructure riding the same session.
6. No credential/browser-data exfiltration payload was observed in this capture (only fingerprint/telemetry data); no lateral movement to other internal hosts was observed — all internal traffic from 10.1.21.58 stayed within normal AD/DNS/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB conversation with the domain controller 10.1.21.2.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / check-in endpoint**
- `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49:80) — plaintext HTTP C2 panel, endpoint `/api/set_agent`
- Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
- Bot token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

**Malicious / suspicious domains**
- `hiyter.com` (104.21.22.231) — initial redirect/landing page
- `media.megafilehub4.lat` (104.21.48.156) — fake file-hosting landing page
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67) — payload delivery host (16 MB download over TLS)
- `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156) — secondary redirect/check-in host
- `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) — fingerprinting/telemetry C2
- `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24) — follow-on redirect infrastructure
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36) — follow-on redirect infrastructure (scareware-style naming)

**Malicious URLs observed**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge` and `...&agent=Edge&act=log` (same id/token)
- `https://arch.filemegahab4.sbs/` (payload delivery; full path/query not recoverable — TLS-encrypted, SNI hidden via Cloudflare ECH)

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No filename or SHA256 hash could be recovered. The only substantial file transfer (16 MB, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` ↔ 10.1.21.58:54840) is entirely inside a TLS session; no cleartext HTTP object export was possible from this capture. All other malicious HTTP traffic (whitepepper.su) is JSON telemetry, not a file transfer.

**Scope note:** benign background traffic to Google/Microsoft/Bing infrastructure, mDNS/LLMNR/SSDP broadcast noise, and normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to 10.1.21.2 were reviewed and excluded as non-indicative.
